strings.title: Dividing with the Area Model
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Divide a three-digit number by a two-digit number with the area model: take out 10 groups first, then see what's left.
strings.keywords: divide, area model, 10 groups, how many groups, quotient, what's left
watchFor: Splitting by place value (156 = 100 + 50 + 6) when those parts don't divide by 12: ask "How much is 10 groups of 12? Start there."
Forgetting to add the parts of the quotient: ask "How many 12s altogether?"
Losing track of what's left: ask "What's 156 − 120?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why did we always start with 10 groups?" Land: 10 times the divisor is easy, so take it out first; then divide what's left and add the parts. The area model shows the side lengths adding up.

problems.notes: Look for: 10 × 12 = 120, 24 left is 2 × 12. Ask: "How many 12s?" Word choice: "how many groups of 12". Model: area 144 / 12 = 120 + 24

responses.say: 10 twelves is 120, 24 left is 2 more twelves. 12.

responses.tip: A fact. Ask: how could you check it?

problems.notes: Look for: 120 + 36. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: area 156 / 12 = 120 + 36

responses.say: 144 is 12 twelves, plus one more 12 is 156. 13.

responses.tip: Forgot the 10 groups in 120. Ask: how many 12s are in 120?

problems.notes: Look for: 140 + 28. Ask: "What's 10 groups of 14?" Model: area 168 / 14 = 140 + 28

responses.tip: Halving both numbers. Ask: why is the answer the same?

problems.notes: Look for: 150 + 45. Ask: "How many 15s in 45?" Model: area 195 / 15 = 150 + 45

responses.say: 200 is 13 fifteens and 5 more, so 195 is 13.

responses.tip: Stopped after 10 groups. Ask: can 45 make more 15s?

problems.notes: Look for: 240 + 48. Ask: "Is there a bigger first chunk?" Model: area 288 / 24 = 240 + 48

responses.tip: Ask: why can we halve both?

problems.notes: Look for: 210 + 42. Ask: "What's the same as 288 ÷ 24?" Model: area 252 / 21 = 210 + 42
Look for: 250 + 50, or 4 quarters in each 100. Ask: "How is this like money?" Model: area 300 / 25 = 250 + 50
